title: Find the Maximum Number of Marked Indices
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array, you can mark pairs of indices i and j if 2 * nums[i] <= nums[j] and both are unmarked.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array, you can mark pairs of indices i and j if 2 * nums[i] <= nums[j] and both are unmarked. Determine the greatest number of indices that can be marked through any number of such operations.
constraints: A marking operation pairs two currently unmarked indices whose values can be ordered as 2*small <= large.
Each index may be marked once.
Return the maximum number of marked indices.
hints: Sort values and reserve a lower half as small candidates and an upper half as large candidates.
Scan large candidates in order, pairing each with the earliest still-unpaired small value it can satisfy.
Advance the small pointer only after a successful pair.
Using the smallest available partner preserves larger small values for later, while the half split guarantees disjoint indices and maximum pair count.
editorial: Using the smallest available partner preserves larger small values for later, while the half split guarantees disjoint indices and maximum pair count.

tests.explanation: After sorting, pair two with four; no second valid disjoint pair exists, so two indices are marked.
Pairs two with five and four with nine mark all four indices.
